topic: Modeling Population Growth: Exponential vs. Logistic
target_audience: High school biology/math students or introductory college ecology students

sections.title: Prerequisites: The Variables of Growth
sections.content: Introduce the foundational variables used in population modeling. Explain 'N' (Population size), 't' (Time), and 'r' (Intrinsic rate of increase). Use a simple visual of a birth-to-death balance scale to explain how 'r' is calculated (Birth rate minus Death rate).
sections.example: A population of 100 rabbits (N=100) where 10 are born and 5 die per year results in an 'r' of 0.05.

sections.title: Exponential Growth: The J-Curve
sections.content: Define exponential growth as population increase under 'ideal' conditions with unlimited resources. Present the differential equation dN/dt = rN. Visually, animate a graph where the line curves upward like the letter 'J'. Emphasize that the more individuals there are, the faster the population grows.
sections.example: A single bacterium dividing every 20 minutes in a nutrient-rich petri dish, rapidly filling the space within hours.

sections.title: The Reality Check: Carrying Capacity (K)
sections.content: Introduce the concept of 'Environmental Resistance.' Explain that in the real world, food, space, and water are limited. Define 'Carrying Capacity' (K) as the maximum population size an environment can sustain indefinitely. Show a horizontal dashed line on the graph labeled 'K'.
sections.example: A small island with a fixed amount of grass that can only support a maximum of 500 deer.

sections.title: Logistic Growth: The S-Curve
sections.content: Introduce the Logistic Growth model: dN/dt = rN * ((K - N) / K). Explain the math visually: when N is small, growth is fast; as N approaches K, the term (K-N)/K becomes zero, stopping growth. Animate the J-curve bending into an 'S' shape as it levels off at the K-line.
sections.example: A group of fish introduced to a new pond. They grow quickly at first, but growth slows and stabilizes as they reach the limit of the pond's food supply.

sections.title: Summary & Comparison
sections.content: Place the J-curve and S-curve side-by-side. Highlight the key difference: Exponential growth assumes infinite resources, while Logistic growth accounts for reality. Use a final animation to show how a population might overshoot K and then settle back down to it.
sections.example: Comparing human population growth in the 20th century (resembling exponential) vs. a balanced forest ecosystem (logistic).
